newsitem.title: USA: Bermuda Commodities Exchange begins trading April.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda Commodities Exchange begins trading April.

text.p: Bermuda Commodities Exchange said Monday it will begin operations in April and will initially trade contracts covering insured homeowners losses resulting from such catastrophes such as hurricanes, tornadoes and winter storms.
The Hamilton, Bermuda-based exchange said its initial members are American International Group Inc, Chase Manhattan Corp and reinsurance intermediary Guy Carpenter & Co Inc.
It said a letter of intent was signed with Chicago Board of Trade to provide services to the new exchange and to offer trading privileges to CBOT members.
All trading will be conducted in U.S. dollars and regulatory supervision will be provided by the Bermuda Monetary Authority, it said.
Thomas Heise, president, said the exchange creates a mechanism "equally attractive to institutions seeking to hedge or invest in catastrophic risk."
The initial products to be traded on the exchange will cover seven geographic areas of the United States. Contracts covering future risk periods will also be offered, it said.
The exchange was created by an act of the Bermuda Parliament. The exchange will be owned by its membes, who will trade contracts that track the Guy Carpenter Castrophe Index.
